attributions.claim: Girgis and colleagues described both cruciates in the same cadaveric work, including the PCL's bundle arrangement and its reciprocal tension pattern through flexion.

Gollehon, Torzilli and Warren ran the sectioning study in the 1980s that cut the PCL and the posterolateral structures in sequence and in combination, measuring posterior translation and external rotation at a range of flexion angles.
Grood and colleagues ran related sectioning work that separated posterior translation from rotation and showed that the two behave differently depending on which structure has gone.
Harner quantified the PCL's cross sectional area and compared the bundles mechanically, which is the anatomical argument behind double bundle reconstruction.
Race and Amis tested PCL bundle function and reconstruction constructs in the 1990s, including the question of whether a single graft can reproduce the reciprocal pattern.
